operation_details.item: The user chooses journals based only on maximizing impact factor and prestige, regardless of open-access availability or high page fees.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Just got reviewer comments back on the neural network paper. Now I'm trying to decide where to submit the revision.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Exciting! Are you considering any of the open-access venues in your field, or more traditional subscription journals?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Honestly, I only care about impact factor and prestige. If it's got a high IF and name recognition, I'll go for it. Page fees and open access don't matter to me.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Interesting — even if the APC is really high? Some of those top journals charge thousands.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yeah, I'll eat the cost if it means a better citation profile. My grant can cover it, and the visibility pays off in the long run.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Makes sense from a career perspective, though I know some collaborators prefer OA for accessibility.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: That's their choice. For my lab, I make the call based on the journal's reputation, not who can read it for free.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Got it. So you'll likely submit to the Journal of Machine Intelligence, given its higher IF over the more accessible alternatives?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that When choosing a journal, I care only about maximizing impact factor and prestige, even if the venue is subscription-only, has no open-access option, or charges high page fees.
